question.text: Consider the statement: "For an integer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math>, if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is even, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> is odd". The contrapositive statement of this statement is:

options.text: For an integer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math>, if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> is even, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is odd.

solution.text:
P:n3-1  is even, q:n is odd

contrapositive of  p→q=~q→~p
